quality_rubric.grounding: Every material transcript-derived conclusion cites canonical segment_ids.
quality_rubric.coverage: Process every exact VIDEO_ID and every requested feature.
quality_rubric.semantic_synthesis: Write semantic summaries that consolidate meaning, argument, method and implications; do not concatenate or lightly rewrite transcript lines.
quality_rubric.timeline: Create boundaries only when the substantive topic changes; merge adjacent fragments about the same point.
quality_rubric.claims: Extract all consequential factual, medical, safety, financial, legal, causal, quantitative and recommendation claims; grade risk and external-verification need.
quality_rubric.entities: Perform named-entity recognition, merge aliases, type entities using the controlled list, and omit generic nouns.
quality_rubric.taxonomy: Use only controlled categories and canonical non-promotional tags.
quality_rubric.editorial: Make assessments specific to this video's evidence, value, limitations and audience; never reuse boilerplate.
quality_rubric.consistency: Use the same canonical evidence across summaries, timeline, claims, intake and editorial assessment.
quality_rubric.specificity: Preserve useful names, quantities, steps and qualifications; avoid generic filler.
quality_rubric.uncertainty: Distinguish source claims, supplied support, interpretation and external-verification needs.
quality_rubric.comments: Cluster only structured supplied comment records and report total, included count and sampling limitations; popularity is not factual verification.
quality_rubric.clips: Select only self-contained clips lasting 30-180 seconds, with valid non-overlapping timestamps and a video-specific purpose.

instructions.instructions: Use only the evidence embedded in this independently processed package and obey response_schema.feature_contracts, controlled_taxonomy, and formal_json_schema. Process every exact VIDEO_ID and return one final JSON object with no prose or markdown. All features must use the same canonical sentence-level transcript segments. For this video, I visited some chemist shops to find out the most frequently bought products by Indians. After thoroughly researching on these products, I have selected 5 products at the chemist shop which needs your immediate attention. I am highly impressed by a few of these products while others are simply a disaster. So, in this video I will be unwrapping 5 products at the chemist shop whose truth I think you should know about.

0:42 - Disclaimer. Whatever I have spoken in this video, is my honest opinion. none of the brands of these 5 products or their competitors have paid me. Just like you, I am consumer looking to buy genuine products for myself and my family.
0:53 - #5 Revital. Revital is among the largest sold supplements for daily vitamins and minerals. But is it worth your hard earned money? Let’s dig in.
02:32 - #4 Safi. Hamdard’s Safi is another popular product at the chemist shop claimed to naturally purify the blood. Most people use it to reduce pimples and get a clear and glowing skin. The company even boasts of it’s 21 days safi challenge. So is this product really worth the craze?
03:58 - #3 Glucon D. Glucon D is probably the most popular energy drink among Indians. Although, is it safe? Can it be consumed on a daily basis. Is it a good intraworkout drink?. To answer these questions, let’s delve into the ingredients. 
05:45 - #2 Strepsils. When we are down with sore throat, cold or cough we look for an instant relief from that uncomfortable feeling. Most of us tend to get our hands on the easily available and convenient strepsils. But are they really good for you? 
07:04 - #1 Kayam Churan.  It’s one of most popular churans used by Indians for chronic constipation and other digestive issues. It is an Ayurvedic product made solely out of herbs. But does that mean it can be consumed daily without any harm? No.
